text:
anna: quick sync - follow-up from the quant RFC: we need a robust strategy for switching precision per-session without longctx/kv surprises. low-noise, low-cost preferred.

lee: recap of failure mode I hit: an fp8 elevation mid-conversation made the server write KV blobs that later consumers (still in int8) tried to read -> nonsense tokens.

rachel: so two levers: prevent cross-precision reuse, or make blobs self-describing + convertible. each has tradeoffs.

ben: preventing reuse easiest: precision fence on session boundaries. If any request in session used higher precision, mark session fenced -> next requests start fresh un-warmed context. But UX hit (cold start) could be large.

anna: agree fence is simple but harsh. we should explore hybrid: maintain per-session precision tag + lightweight inline conversion on read when possible.

infra-bot: note: serializer v2 has fields for model/version; we can add a tiny footer with quant-format and a checksum. header/footer change cheap but must be backward compatible.

lee: conversion-on-read idea: when int8 reader sees fp8 blob, attempt to re-quantize KV into int8 on the fly, then validate with a checksum or small token replay. If validation fails, fall back to compute from scratch.

rachel: conversion adds CPU cost and potential error. re-quantization heuristics need careful testing. For keys that represent attention caches, do we preserve exact alignment?

ben: maybe limit conversion to small KV entries (prefix caches, short history). For large longctx blocks, refuse conversion and trigger session fence. That reduces rare cold starts but keeps correctness.

anna: proposal: three-tier policy: 1) exact-match precision: use blob as-is. 2) convertible small-blobs: attempt conversion-on-read + validate by replaying N tokens (N configurable). 3) incompatible/large blobs: treat as miss and optionally trigger 'soft-fence' (drop KV but keep session id).

ops: we need metrics for soft-fence impact. soft-fence should emit event `precision.soft_fence` with session, model, reason. Also track % of reads in tier2 vs tier3.

jamal: runtime impl notes: add blob footer `QUANT:fp8;LEN:12345;CK:abcd1234;V:3`. Reader checks QUANT. If mismatch -> if LEN < convert_threshold then spawn requant task inline with time budget. else miss.

infra-bot: migration concern: older nodes will ignore footer. So write nodes must write footer only when feature-flagged. Readers behind flag can parse. Two-step rollout required.

lee: edge-case: two concurrent sessions on same user, one elevated to fp8 and one normal. If they share cached prefix due to same prompt, we must ensure isolation. session-scoped namespace seems necessary anyway.

rachel: yes namespace keys by session_id or by a session-isolation bit when session override requested. That avoids cross-session bleed but increases footprint for heavy session usage.

ben: optimization: only namespace overlay for delta writes. The base cache remains global. Overlay entries reference base keys and store small conversion metadata. So memory growth = number of overlays, not full duplication.

anna: that aligns with our 'overlay' idea but phrased as session delta store + convert-on-read fallback. good compromise.

ops: rollout plan suggestion: 1) add footer schema and flag-wrapped writes 2) readers parse footer and log mismatches but treat as miss 3) enable conversion-on-read for len<threshold on canary nodes 4) enable session-overlay writes 5) enable client SDK header for session override

jamal: also add response meta `x-precision-applied` with value {requested:fp8,effective:int8,actions:[converted]}. keep it compact.

infra-bot: perf note: inline conversion must be bounded. Suggest 50ms budget; if hit, abort conversion and mark miss. Measure tail latency delta in canary.

rachel: quality gating: we need offline per-model probe sets to decide which prompts are safe for fp8 transitions. runtime can't be perfect; allowlist + customer opt-in.

anna: agreed. add `quality_allowlist` config per customer/model and telemetry alerts when conversions correlate with quality drops.

ben: decision? sounds like: implement footer + parsing -> session-overlay namespace -> conversion-on-read for small blobs with strict timeout -> soft-fence for large mismatches. Rollout behind feature flags and canary.

ops: i'll draft canary playbook and dashboards for `precision.*` events. include capacity bump estimate for overlay memory.

lee: i'll prototype the conversion logic and unit tests for checksum + replay validation.

anna: thanks folks. i'll write the RFC follow-up with the three-tier policy, schema examples, and rollout steps. ping when drafts ready. :thumbsup:
